rationale: Spring MVC controller exposing a single GET /oups endpoint that deliberately throws an exception to demonstrate the error view. It is part of the HTTP surface, but it is a demo/showcase endpoint with no business value, so its architectural significance is minor.

An HTTP POST route for editing a pet is an API operation on the system boundary. It validates the form, persists the update through updatePetDetails (handling DataIntegrityViolationException), and drives the MVC UI by returning a form view or a redirect with a flash message.

Spring MVC controller for the vet domain. It serves an HTML vet list view with pagination and a JSON /vets resource endpoint. As a class grouping several handlers, it is best modelled as an application component at the system boundary. It drives the web UI via Thymeleaf views; persistence is delegated to VetRepository.

Owner is a core JPA domain entity with validated properties and a one-to-many relationship to Pet. It is the canonical entity schema for owners, central to the petclinic domain. Its JPA annotations only map it to a table; the entity itself does not perform reads or writes, which repositories do.

Spring Data repository interface defining the read-only, cached query access to Vet records (findAll, paged findAll). It is the persistence access layer for the vets collection, a significant data-store element documenting how the application reads vet data.

Spring MVC formatter component that converts PetType values to and from strings for form binding. It looks pet types up through the repository, but persistence itself is delegated. This is an internal conversion function, a minor framework-glue unit rather than a service or contract.

Spring @Bean factory method that configures the framework's session-based LocaleResolver with an English default. It is small framework configuration (i18n setup) rather than application behaviour. Session storage is in-memory HTTP session state, not durable persistence. Minor configuration significance.

A trivial getter on the Person entity that returns a field value. The Person entity may be modelled in the data model, but this accessor is boilerplate and not an architectural element in its own right. It implements no cross-cutting concern.

A Spring MVC GET handler for /owners/find that returns the findOwners view name. It is an HTTP route endpoint, so it is modelled as an API operation. It drives the UI by selecting the view to render. The logic is trivial, so its significance is moderate.

This is a small domain-entity method on Owner. It validates its inputs, looks up the pet and delegates adding the visit to Pet. That is aggregate-internal behaviour, not an element an architecture model would record on its own. It does no persistence itself, because saving happens through the repository in the controller.

Constructor that only injects the OwnerRepository dependency into VisitController. It is trivial dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own. The controller class itself would be modelled, but this constructor is not a separate architectural element.

A boilerplate toString override on the Owner entity that formats its fields for debugging. It is a trivial formatting helper with no architectural role, so it would not be recorded as a model element.

A private controller helper that builds a fixed-size Pageable and delegates to OwnerRepository. It is a small pagination implementation detail, used only by processFindForm. It does not access storage itself; the repository it calls does that.

A trivial collection mutator on the Pet entity that appends a Visit to its visits list. It is an implementation detail of the entity's data model. It is not architecturally meaningful on its own, and it performs no persistence directly.

A Spring Data repository query method with a JPQL @Query that reads all PetTypes ordered by name. It is a documented read access pattern against the persistence store and is used by the controller, the formatter and the tests. Notable within the repository but not a standalone component.

Spring configuration enabling JCache caching and creating the 'vets' cache with JMX statistics. This is infrastructure/platform configuration providing a caching technology service. It is in-memory, not durable storage. Enabling statistics is a minor observability aspect. It is a notable infrastructure unit, but small in scope.

A Spring @Bean factory method that configures the framework's LocaleChangeInterceptor with the 'lang' parameter. This is small framework configuration boilerplate inside WebConfiguration, not an architectural element in its own right. It only supports i18n locale switching, so it is minor.

A trivial Spring Formatter method that returns the PetType name, or a placeholder when it is null. It is a formatting implementation detail with no architectural weight of its own, below the level an architecture model would record.

This is GraalVM native-image runtime hints registration boilerplate. It registers resource patterns and reflection types for AOT compilation. It is build and runtime configuration scaffolding, not an architecturally meaningful application element. Its small role in native packaging gives it minimal significance.

A private helper that builds a JCache MutableConfiguration with statistics enabled and is used only by the cache customizer. The enclosing CacheConfiguration class is the architecturally relevant element; this one-line factory is an implementation detail with no cross-cutting work of its own.

An @XmlElement accessor on the Vet entity. It exposes the specialties relationship as a serialized property, returning the specialties sorted by name. It is a minor property-level element of the domain schema and does not perform any persistence I/O itself.

Spring MVC controller mapped to /owners/{ownerId} that exposes the pet create and update HTTP endpoints. It drives server-rendered form views and delegates persistence to the repositories. As the web boundary for pet management it is best modelled as an API path grouping, and it is architecturally significant.

A Spring @Bean that registers the 'vets' JCache cache via a JCacheManagerCustomizer. It is infrastructure configuration for the caching technology service, named when explaining the caching setup. It configures cache storage rather than doing business logic, so it is classed as technology.

Spring Data JPA repository for Owner entities defining query methods (last-name prefix search with paging, find by id). It is the persistence access layer for owners, an architecturally significant data access component documenting how the application reads owner data.

GraalVM native-image runtime hints registrar: build/deployment configuration that registers resource patterns and reflection types for AOT compilation. It is platform/build configuration rather than application behaviour, so it fits technology as a configuration artifact. It has minor architectural significance and implements no cross-cutting concern.

This is the default constructor of the Visit entity. It only initialises the date field to tomorrow. That is an implementation detail of the entity class rather than an architectural element in its own right. The Visit class itself would be modelled in the data-model layer.

A trivial JavaBean getter on the Person entity that returns a field. The Person entity itself would belong in the data model, but this accessor is boilerplate with no architectural meaning of its own.

Spring MVC POST handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/new. It validates the visit date, adds the visit to the owner, saves via the repository and redirects with a flash message. As an HTTP route handler it maps to an API operation. It persists data and drives the web UI form flow.

Domain entity method on Owner that maintains the in-memory Owner-Pet relationship with duplicate guards. It is a minor behavior of the data-model entity rather than a standalone architectural element. It does not itself write to storage; JPA cascade handles persistence elsewhere.

This is a Spring MVC POST handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/new, so it is an API operation. It validates the pet form (duplicate name, future birth date) and persists the owner via saveAndFlush. It also drives the UI by returning a view name or a redirect with a flash message.

A JPA @MappedSuperclass domain base type that adds a validated name property to BaseEntity. It is a shared entity schema building block that PetType, Specialty and similar entities inherit. The JPA annotations only map columns; the class performs no storage I/O itself. It is notable within the model package but not a core architectural boundary.

A trivial @ModelAttribute helper that supplies tomorrow's date to the view model as the minimum visit date. It is a one-line implementation detail of VisitController. It does no persistence, makes no external calls and renders nothing itself, so it is not an architecturally meaningful element on its own.

A JAXB-annotated wrapper DTO holding a list of Vet entities, used to serialize the vets resource response. It is a simple response data shape with minor significance. It does no persistence or integration work itself.

An HTTP POST endpoint handling new visit form submission. It validates the visit date, persists the owner via the repository, and drives the MVC view, either redisplaying the form or redirecting. It is a primary API operation of the petclinic visit booking workflow.

This is an HTTP GET endpoint in the Spring MVC OwnerController that serves the owner edit form. It is modelled as an API operation. It drives the web UI by returning a view name, does no persistence itself, and is a routine CRUD form endpoint of moderate significance.

A trivial JavaBean setter on the Owner entity that only assigns a field. The city property belongs to the Owner data model, but the setter method itself is boilerplate. It is not an architecturally meaningful element on its own.

Constructor that only performs dependency injection of VetRepository into VetController. It is boilerplate wiring with no behaviour of its own; the controller class itself is the meaningful element, not this constructor.

An HTTP GET route in Spring MVC PetClinic that serves the new-visit form view. It is an API operation on the web surface and drives the user interface by returning a template name. It performs no persistence, because the model attributes are populated elsewhere.

Trivial derived getter on the Vet entity that returns the size of its specialties collection. It is an implementation detail of the entity, not an architectural element in its own right, and it implements no cross-cutting concern.

HTTP GET /owners route handler in Spring MVC controller; an API operation that searches owners by last name with pagination and returns server-rendered views or redirects. It drives the web UI via view names; persistence is delegated to the repository through a helper method.

A GET /oups route handler that deliberately throws a RuntimeException to demonstrate error handling. It is an HTTP endpoint, so it models as an API operation, but it is a demo/showcase endpoint with no business logic, which gives it moderate significance.

Spring MVC controller exposing GET / that returns the 'welcome' view name. It is an HTTP route handler and thus an API operation. Its role is simple but it is the application's landing entry point, and it drives the user-facing welcome page.

Trivial Spring Validator boilerplate override that checks whether a class is assignable to Pet. It is an implementation detail of PetValidator, not an architecturally meaningful element on its own, and implements no cross-cutting concern.

A GET /vets route handler with @ResponseBody that returns the vet list as JSON/XML is a REST API operation. Its only persistence work is a call to the repository's findAll, and calling it does not count as the method implementing persistence itself. It is a public API contract endpoint.

A trivial JavaBean setter on the Visit entity that only assigns a field. It is boilerplate below the level an architecture model would record. The Visit entity itself would be modelled in the data-model layer, not its accessors.

HTTP GET /oups route in PetClinic's CrashController. It deliberately throws a RuntimeException to demonstrate the error page. It is an API operation, but a demo-only endpoint with no business logic, so its significance is low.

Trivial JPA entity setter on Pet that assigns a field. It is boilerplate accessor code with no behaviour of its own. The Pet entity would be modelled, but this method is not an architectural element and implements no cross-cutting concern.

A trivial accessor on BaseEntity that reports whether the id is null. It is a small helper method inside a data-model entity, not an architectural element on its own. It touches no storage, I/O or other cross-cutting concern.

A private helper that fills the Spring MVC model with pagination attributes and returns the vet list view name. It is an implementation detail of the showVetList handler, not a standalone architectural element. It does prepare data for rendering the UI view.

A JPA @MappedSuperclass domain entity that defines the shared firstName/lastName properties and their validation constraints for Owner and Vet. It is a canonical domain schema shape, so it is an objectschema in the data model. It has moderate significance as a base type, and it does no persistence I/O itself.

Spring Data derived query method on OwnerRepository defining a paginated prefix search on owners by last name. It is a documented data access pattern against the owners table, used by the owner search controller. It is notable but not a standalone component.

Spring MVC controller for booking pet visits. It serves HTML form views, so it is not a REST API contract; it is best modelled as an application component. It drives the web UI by choosing view templates and setting flash messages. Persistence is delegated to OwnerRepository, so data_persistence is false.

Spring Boot bootstrap entry point that launches the PetClinic application. It is the process entry, but it is a one-line boilerplate delegation to SpringApplication.run. The architectural element is really the enclosing PetClinicApplication component, so this method is moderately significant.

A trivial collection mutator on the Vet entity that appends a Specialty to its internal set. It is an implementation detail of the entity, not an architectural element on its own, and it does not persist anything directly.

HTTP POST endpoint for creating a new pet under an owner. It forms part of the API surface. It validates input and persists the owner via the repository (saveAndFlush). It drives the web UI by returning a view name or a redirect with a flash message.

A trivial JavaBean setter on the Pet entity that only assigns a field. The Pet entity itself belongs in the data model, but this accessor is boilerplate with no behaviour of its own and is not a modelled element.

HTTP GET route in Spring MVC PetController that initializes a new Pet for an owner and returns the create/update form view. It is an API operation on the web surface. It drives the UI by rendering a server-side form, and it does not persist anything.

Spring MVC GET /owners route handler implementing the owner search operation: it normalizes the last name, queries paginated results, and selects a view or redirect. As an HTTP endpoint it belongs in the API layer, and it drives the UI by choosing views. Persistence is delegated to a helper.

Constructor of PetTypeFormatter that simply assigns the injected PetTypeRepository dependency to a field. This is trivial dependency-injection boilerplate with no behaviour of its own, so it is not an architectural element.

Spring @InitBinder hook that stops 'id' fields from being bound from the request, a guard against mass assignment. It is a one-line, controller-local configuration detail. It is not an endpoint or a standalone security policy, so it would not be modelled as its own architecture element.

Trivial getter on the Owner entity returning the city field. It is boilerplate accessor code with no logic. The Owner entity itself would be modeled in the data-model layer, but this accessor is not an architectural element on its own.

A trivial getter on the NamedEntity base class that returns the name field. It has no logic of its own. The entity class itself belongs in the data model, but the accessor is an implementation detail that would not be recorded as an architecture element.

Spring MVC GET handler for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/edit that returns the pet create/update form view name. As a route handler it is an API operation. It is simple but a named endpoint, and it drives the web UI by selecting the view to render.
Trivial getter on the Pet entity that returns the type field. The Pet entity itself belongs in the data model, but this accessor is an implementation detail with no architectural meaning on its own.

Vet is a core JPA domain entity in the petclinic model, inheriting Person and holding a many-to-many relationship to Specialty. It defines a domain record shape, best modelled as a data-model object schema. It is mapped to the vets table but performs no storage I/O itself.

The symbol is an HTTP GET route, /owners/new, in a Spring MVC controller, so it is modelled as an API operation. It returns the owner create/update form view, so it drives the web UI. It is a simple endpoint with no persistence or security logic, which keeps its significance moderate.

This is Spring MVC configuration boilerplate that registers the locale change interceptor with the framework registry. It is a one-line override inside WebConfiguration with no behaviour of its own, so it is not an architecturally meaningful element on its own.

A trivial JPA entity setter on Visit that assigns a field. It is boilerplate accessor code with no behaviour of its own. The Visit entity itself would be modelled in the data-model layer, but this method is not an architectural element on its own.

A trivial JavaBean getter on the Pet entity that returns the birthDate field. It is part of the entity's data shape, but it is not an architectural element on its own. The birthDate property would be modelled on the Pet entity, not as a method.

Trivial getter on the Pet entity returning its visits collection. The Pet-Visit relationship would be modelled at the entity level, not through this accessor. It is an implementation detail with no logic and no cross-cutting concerns.

Trivial toString override on the NamedEntity base class that returns the name or a null placeholder. This is formatting boilerplate with no architectural role; the listed callers are largely unrelated toString resolutions from the call graph.

Spring MVC GET / handler that returns the 'welcome' view name. It is an HTTP route handler, so it is modelled as an API operation. It is the application's landing entry point but trivial in logic. It drives UI rendering by selecting a Thymeleaf view.

HTTP GET route /owners/{ownerId} exposed by OwnerController. It loads an Owner via the repository and renders the ownerDetails view. This is a public endpoint of the PetClinic web surface, so it is modelled as an API operation. It touches persistence through findById and drives a server-rendered UI.

Pet is a core JPA domain entity in the petclinic model. It defines properties (birthDate, type) and relationships to PetType and Visit, so it is best modelled as an entity schema. The ORM mapping is declarative; the class itself performs no storage I/O, so data_persistence is false.

Protected lazy-initialising getter on the Vet entity that returns the internal specialties set. It is a trivial accessor used only within its own class and is not architecturally meaningful on its own.

Trivial getter on the BaseEntity JPA superclass that returns the id field. The entity itself would be modelled in the data model, but this accessor is boilerplate with no behaviour of its own and no architectural significance.

HTTP GET /vets route returning a JSON/XML Vets resource body. It is a REST API operation on the system boundary. It calls the repository, but persistence is delegated to it, so no concern is flagged for the route itself.

A Spring @ModelAttribute pre-handler that loads the owner and pet through the repository, populates the MVC model, and creates a new Visit. It is internal controller support behaviour rather than an endpoint itself. Persistence is delegated to OwnerRepository, so the data_persistence concern is false.

Spring @InitBinder configuration hook that wires PetValidator into the pet form binder and disallows binding of id fields. This is framework boilerplate supporting the controller, not a standalone architectural element. The validator itself would be the element worth modelling.
Trivial getter on the Visit entity that returns a field. The Visit entity itself would be modelled in the data model, but this accessor is boilerplate with no architectural meaning of its own.

A lazily-initializing getter on the Vets XML wrapper DTO. It is trivial accessor boilerplate with an @XmlElement annotation for serialization. The architecturally meaningful element is the parent Vets class, not this method.

Trivial JavaBean getter on the Owner entity that returns a field. It is an implementation detail of the data model and not an architectural element on its own. The telephone property would be modelled as part of the Owner entity schema instead.

A Spring Data JPA repository query method that retrieves an Owner by its primary key. It is a data-store access pattern used widely by the controllers, and it reads durable storage. It is a single method rather than the repository itself, so it rates moderate significance.

This is the Spring Boot application entry point (main method plus @SpringBootApplication) that bootstraps the whole PetClinic system. It represents the deployable application component and is the core entry point. The class itself implements none of the cross-cutting concerns.

A private helper in VetController that builds a Pageable with a fixed page size and delegates to VetRepository.findAll. It is a pagination implementation detail of the list handler, not an architectural element. It does no persistence work itself; the repository does.

A trivial JavaBean getter on the Visit entity that returns the description field. The Visit entity itself would be modelled; this accessor is boilerplate with no behaviour of its own, so it is not an architectural element.

Spring Data repository query method that reads paginated Vets from the database. It is read-only, transactional and cached. As a documented read access pattern on the vets collection, it is a notable unit within the persistence layer, though only one method of the repository.

PetType is a JPA domain entity mapped to the 'types' table and inheriting name/id from NamedEntity. It is a domain type definition (a lookup entity: Cat, Dog, etc.), so it belongs in the data-model layer as an object schema. It has no behaviour, and persistence is handled by the framework rather than by this class itself.

Trivial JavaBean setter on the Person entity. It only assigns a field and has no logic. As an implementation detail below the level an architecture model records, it has no layer or element type and carries no cross-cutting concerns.

JPA @MappedSuperclass that defines the identity property shared by all PetClinic domain entities. It is the central base of the domain model's entity hierarchy. It holds only a mapping annotation and does no persistence work itself, so it is modelled as a data-model object schema.

A Spring Data JPA repository for PetType entities, with a custom JPQL query that retrieves pet types ordered by name. It is the persistence access layer for a domain aggregate, so it belongs in the data-store layer and models best as a documented access pattern.

A JPA @Entity mapped to the 'specialties' table, representing the Vet specialty domain entity. It is a domain type (an object schema) inheriting name and id from NamedEntity. It has no behaviour of its own, and persistence is performed by repositories, not by this class.

Visit is a JPA domain entity mapped to the 'visits' table, with validated fields (date, description). It is a core domain type in the petclinic model, best recorded as a data-model object schema. The ORM mapping annotations make it part of persistence.

HTTP GET route in Spring MVC PetController serving the pet edit form view; it is an endpoint on the system's web surface, modelled as an API operation. It returns a view name for rendering a UI form, so it drives the user interface. It performs no persistence directly.

A trivial JavaBean setter on the Owner entity. It only assigns a field and has no logic of its own. The Owner entity may warrant modelling, but this accessor is boilerplate below the level an architecture model would record.

An HTTP POST route handler for creating owners is an API operation. It validates form input, persists the owner via the repository, and drives the MVC UI by returning a view or redirect with flash messages. It is a significant system boundary endpoint for a core workflow.

Formatter parse method converting a form text value into a PetType by looking it up through the repository. This is minor internal conversion logic within the Spring formatter. Persistence happens in the repository it calls, not in this method, so no concern applies directly.

Trivial setter on the BaseEntity identifier field. It holds no logic and performs no persistence itself; persistence comes from the JPA mapping, not this method. It is an implementation detail of the entity, not an architectural element.

A Spring @Configuration class wiring the i18n framework infrastructure: a session-based locale resolver and a locale-change interceptor. It is framework configuration rather than business logic, so it is modelled as a technology configuration artifact. It drives user-facing language selection, hence the UI concern.

HTTP GET / route in Spring MVC WelcomeController that returns the 'welcome' view name. It is an HTTP operation on the app's surface and serves as the landing page entry point, though it is trivial in logic. Modelled as an API operation that drives the UI.

A trivial JavaBean setter on the Person entity. It only assigns a field and has no logic. The Person entity itself belongs to the data model, but this accessor is boilerplate and not an architectural element on its own.

HTTP GET endpoint /owners/find in the Spring MVC OwnerController that returns the 'owners/findOwners' view to display the owner search form. It is part of the HTTP surface, so it is modelled as an API operation. It is a simple form-entry endpoint with no business logic, so its significance is moderate.

The method is the Spring MVC handler for GET /vets.html, so it is modelled as an API operation. It validates the page parameter, redirects when the page is out of range, and populates the view model that renders the paginated vet list. Persistence is delegated to findPaginated, so it does not count as a concern here.

A trivial setter on the NamedEntity base class that only assigns a field. It is boilerplate accessor code with no architectural meaning of its own. The entity class itself would be modelled in the data-model layer, but this method would not.

Spring Validator enforcing Pet form business rules (required name, max length, type, birth date). It is internal application behavior that PetController uses during data binding. It is a notable unit in the owner module but not a core boundary, and it implements none of the listed cross-cutting concerns.

This method implements the Spring Validator contract for Pet domain objects. It applies business validation rules: name is required and limited in length, type is required for new pets, and birth date is required. It is internal application behaviour that a maintainer would name when explaining the owner module. It is not security or persistence logic.
